Mahabubnagar Dt And ... vs The State Of

sentences.text:
(per The Hon'ble Sri Justice K.SURENDER) Appeal is filed by appellants/Accused aggrieved by the conviction recorded by the Special Sessions Judge-cum-VII Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar, in S.C.No.42 of 2014, for the offences under Sections 376(2)(g) and 306 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3(i)(xi) and 3(2)(v) of the SCs/STs (POA) Act, 1989.

entities.text:
Special Sessions Judge-cum-VII Additional District Judge,
Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and Sri D.Arun Kumar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent State.
3.
Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 01.01.2013 at 8.00 P.M., PW.15-S.I of Police received message about the victim/deceased being brought to the hospital with burn injuries.
PW.15 recorded the statement of the deceased.
In the statement given to PW.15, the victim stated that she is a resident of Damarlabanda Thanda, Nawabpet Mandal.
She was married to PW.3 and had two children.
Twenty days prior, two persons namely Chandraiah and Chakali Sathyam who are residents of Kollur village called her for coolie work and forcibly committed rape on her in the cotton fields.
She informed about the incident to her father and village elders, but, none of them responded.
On 01.01.2013, the husband of the deceased-PW.3 returned from Pune and when the deceased informed him about the incident, there was no response by PW.3.
The victim/deceased was disgusted with the conduct of the villagers and also her husband.
She doused herself with Kerosene and set fire to herself.

On the basis of statement (Ex.P17) made, crime was registered under Sections 376(2)(g), 306 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(2)(v) of the SCs/STs (POA)
Act.
4.
A requisition was also given to the jurisdictional Magistrate to record the Dying Declaration.
Learned Magistrate-PW.11 went to the hospital and recorded the statement (Ex.P8) of the deceased on the same day.
The proceedings concluded at 6:40 p.m.

In the said Dying Declaration she narrated as follows;
"Three persons together raped me.
Their names are Chandraiah, Chakali Sathyam and one more person whose name I do not know.
All the three persons raped me from 12:00 noon to 6:00 p.m.
The rape took place at Thimmayyapalli, Nawabpet Mandal.
Thereafter, I consumed rat poison and was treated in Government hospital.
After I recovered I went home.
I also informed the Police about the incident, but nobody responded.
I returned back to Nawabpet.
Again the three persons raped me.

sentences.text: 1 Thereafter, unable to bear the said acts of the three persons, I poured Kerosene on to myself and lit fire.
The statement is voluntary, without anybody's influence."
(translated by me)

5. The police on the basis of the complaint, identified the appellants herein whose names are Godugu Sathaiah s/o.Godugu Somaiah and Godugu Ramaswamy s/o.Ramachandraiah as the two persons who were named by the deceased in her statement to the Police and also in the statement made before the Magistrate.
6. The Investigating Officer had explained regarding the confusion in the names and also the specific identity of the persons named by the deceased in both the statements.
According to the Investigating Officer, under a state of confusion, A2's father's name was stated as his name and the person's name was stated as father's name.

7. Learned Counsel appearing for the appellants mainly argued on two grounds.
i) That the parents of the deceased have turned hostile to the prosecution case and did not speak anything about the rape being committed.
ii) The identity of the persons named by the deceased was wrongly determined and the appellants herein were falsely implicated.
8.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor on the other hand admitted that as seen from the record,
the names are different.
However he argued that there is no reason as to why the Investigating Officer would falsely implicate two innocent villagers as the persons named by the deceased.
9. According to the statement of the victim, three persons had committed rape on her and she has named two persons and also gave the name of the father of one person.
In the statement recorded by PW.5, she stated as Chandraiah s/o.Ramaswamy and Chakali Sathyam.
In the Dying Declaration-Ex.P8, she stated as Chandraiah and Chakali Sathyam without giving any other particulars.
According to the deceased, though she complained about commission of rape by three persons, however, none of the village elders or the husband had taken any action.

None of the witnesses have stated that Chandraiah and Chakali Sathyam referred by the deceased in her statement are the same persons known as Godugu Sathaiah and Godugu Ramaswamy, who are the appellants herein.
10. The Investigating Officer is a stranger to the accused prior to the investigation.
If at all, there were any alias names of the appellants, the same ought to have been adduced during the course of trial from the villagers and also during investigation.
The Investigating Officer himself assuming that the deceased might have wrongly stated the names and implicating the appellants herein is illegal.
There is no connecting link to the identity of the appellants herein.
The victim gave statement to the Police, Magistrate and thereafter she died.
The appellants were not arrested before the death of the deceased or shown to the deceased while she was in the hospital.

sentences.text: Once the identity was not established by the prosecution conclusively that the persons mentioned by the deceased are the appellants herein and they are one and the same, on the basis of assumption that the appellants might be the persons who have committed rape and convicting the appellants, is improper and incorrect.

12. Since the prosecution has failed to prove that rape was committed by the appellants herein and appellants are the persons named by the deceased in her statement/Dying Declaration to PW.15-S.I of Police and learned Magistrate-PW.11 under Exs.P17 and 18, the appeal deserves to be allowed.
13. Accordingly, Conviction recorded by the Special Sessions Judge in S.C.No.42 of 2014 is hereby set aside.
Criminal Appeal is allowed and the appellants/accused are acquitted.
Since the appellants are on bail, their bail bonds shall stand discharged.
